items.text: Cases where descent data are effective
$S'\to S$ faithfully flat quasi-compact; $X'=\bigcup X'_i$ with $X'_i$ stable and affine over $S'$ $\Rightarrow$ the descent datum is effective.
For $S$ affine: effective $\iff$ $X'$ is covered by stable opens affine over $S'$ (the real difficulty is to construct them).
Case 1: radicial base change
$g$ faithfully flat, quasi-compact and radicial: a universal homeomorphism; $q_1,q_2\colon X''\rightrightarrows X'$ agree on underlying sets, so every open of $X'$ is stable.
Reduce to $S$ affine and $S'$ affine (finite disjoint sum $\bar S'$ of affines); then descent data on $X'$ are effective (cover by stable affine opens). E.g. $k'/k$ purely inseparable.
Fails for separable extensions: a degree-two extension and a proper smooth $X'$ over $k'$, not projective, with non-effective descent data.
Case 2: a very ample sheaf with descent data
Descent datum on a pair $(X',\mathcal L')$, $\mathcal L'$ ample relative to $S'$, i.e. $p_1^*\mathcal L'\simeq p_2^*\mathcal L'$ on $X''$ with cocycle condition on $X'''$.
Take $\mathcal L'$ very ample: $\mathcal E'=f'_*\mathcal L'$ quasi-coherent, $f'^*\mathcal E'\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal L'$ and
i'\colon X'\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(\mathcal E')\ \text{an immersion (retrocompact)}
p_1^*\mathcal E'=f''_*q_1^*\mathcal L'\simeq f''_*q_2^*\mathcal L'=p_2^*\mathcal E'\quad(\text{flat base change; cocycle from }\mathcal L'')

So $\mathcal E'$ has descent data and descends to $\mathcal E$ on $S$; $\mathbf P(\mathcal E')=\mathbf P(\mathcal E)'$; $X'\subset\mathbf P'$ is stable, so descends to a subscheme $X\subset\mathbf P(\mathcal E)$; $\mathcal L'$ descends to a very ample $\mathcal L$.
Theorem. $g$ faithfully flat quasi-compact is of 2-descent for pairs $(X',\mathcal L')$, $\mathcal L'$ very ample relative to $S'$.
Corollary: finite locally free base change

$g\colon S'\to S$ faithfully flat, finite and locally free ($S'=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A'$, $\mathcal A'$ locally free of rank $\neq0$); $X'$ quasi-projective over $S'$ with descent data relative to $S$ $\Rightarrow$ the data are effective and $X$ is quasi-projective over $S$.
Need $\mathcal L'$ very ample with descent data: start with $\mathcal M'$ ample on $X'$ and take the norm
\mathcal L'=N_{q_2}\bigl(q_1^*\mathcal M'\bigr)\qquad(\text{saturation of }\mathcal M'\text{ by the equivalence relation }X'')
Norm for $T'=\operatorname{Spec}B\to T$, $B$ locally free over $\mathcal O_T$:
N\colon B\to\mathcal O_T,\quad N(x)=\det(\text{left multiplication by }x),\qquad N(xy)=N(x)N(y),\ N(1)=1,\ \ N\colon B^*\to\mathcal O_T^*

A torsor under $B^*$ (= an invertible $\mathcal O_{T'}$-module) goes to a torsor under $\mathcal O_T^*$ (an invertible $\mathcal O_T$-module): the norm of an invertible sheaf; stable under base change, and ampleness is preserved.
Principle of the finite extension

$X$ over $k$, $X_{k'}$ quasi-projective $\Rightarrow$ $X$ quasi-projective: $k'=\varinjlim A_i$ ($A_i$ of finite type over $k$); $X_{A_i}$ quasi-projective for $i$ large (ample sheaves pass to the limit).
A_i\to k''=A_i/\mathfrak m\ \text{(finite over }k\text{, Nullstellensatz)}:\quad X_{k''}\ \text{quasi-projective}\ \Rightarrow\ X\ \text{quasi-projective by finite flat descent}
Principle: a property of finite presentation stable under base change that holds after some extension holds after a finite extension (isomorphic schemes, surjective morphisms, group structures).
Descent data from a group action
$G$ a group scheme over $S$ acting on $S'$ so that $S'$ is a pseudo-torsor (simply transitive):
S'\times G\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }S'\times_SS',\qquad(x,g)\mapsto(x,xg)
A gluing datum on $X'$ over $S'$: $\pi_{X'}\colon X'\times G\to X'$ over $\pi_{S'}$ with cartesian square.
\begin{CD} X'\times G @>{\pi_{X'}}>> X'\\ @V{f'\times\mathrm{id}}VV @VV{f'}V\\ S'\times G @>{\pi_{S'}}>> S' \end{CD}
It is a descent datum iff $\pi_{X'}$ is associative: a right action of $G$ on $X'$ compatible with $X'\to S'$.
$G=\Gamma_S$ constant: descent data = an action of the abstract group $\Gamma$ (Galois group of $S'/S$) on $X'$ compatible with its action on $S'$.
If $S'\to S$ is of 1-descent: $X\mapsto(X',\text{action of }\Gamma)$ is fully faithful; effectivity is a separate question.
